THE BEGINNER LEARNING PATH

Meme 101A · Foundations

Read the token. Understand the people behind it.

Like penny-stock speculation, micro-tokens mix thin markets, promotion, and concentrated ownership. Global, round-the-clock on-chain trading can compress the cycle. Bots, launchpads, programmable token rules, migration, and copy trading can accelerate it further.

Eight levels, from the first numbers on a token page to planning an exit. Start at Level 1, or choose the question you want to understand.

Start Level 1 →8 foundation levels · dev and bundles in 101C
KEEP ONE QUESTION IN VIEW

Who owns the supply, what did they pay for it, what are they doing now, and who will buy it from them?

LEVEL 1

Read the Token

Learn the basic numbers shown on a meme-token page before looking at narratives, charts, or wallets.

Open lesson ↗LEVEL 2

Understand the Launch

Understand how a meme token moves from creation into active trading and why launch mechanics affect early risk.

Open lesson ↗LEVEL 3

Understand Ownership

Learn who really controls the token supply and whether apparent decentralization is genuine.

Open lesson ↗LEVEL 4

Read Wallets

Move beyond holder percentages and understand what important wallets are actually doing.

Open lesson ↗LEVEL 5

Read Price Behavior

Understand what the chart is showing about supply, demand, and changing valuation.

Open lesson ↗LEVEL 6

Understand Attention

Understand why people notice a meme token and how attention turns into — or fails to turn into — demand.

Open lesson ↗LEVEL 7

Detect Danger

Recognize structural and behavioral risks that can destroy a trade regardless of the narrative.

Open lesson ↗LEVEL 8

Trade and Survive

Turn all previous knowledge into practical risk management.

Open lesson ↗

Dev, bundles & supply

Open 101C · Understand the Dev & Supply → for the full investigation of creator powers, inventory, earnings, and the buyer relationship.

Next: Survival & Hygiene

Continue to 101B → before moving into the applied tracks.

Put the questions to work

Use Snipe for launch context, Swing to compare observed tokens, Inspect for sampled swaps, and Tweet for attention evidence. Wallet clusters, cost basis, and contract permissions may need external research; these lessons do not imply that Meme Fast measures every concept.
